category.name: Customer account takeover & fraud
category.description: Abuse of customer-facing accounts and checkout: credential stuffing, takeover, payment and refund fraud, bots, brand impersonation, and fake accounts.

playbooks.name: Credential stuffing against customer login
playbooks.summary: Use when the customer login endpoint sees a surge of failed logins across many usernames from rotating IPs, with a small success rate that indicates reused breached passwords.

preparation: Log every customer login attempt with username, IP, ASN, user agent, and result
Put bot management or a WAF rate limit in front of login and token endpoints
Check new and changed customer passwords against a breached-password corpus
Agree with product who can turn on step-up challenges during an attack
identification: Chart login failure rate and distinct usernames per minute against the normal baseline
Group attacking traffic by ASN, user agent, and TLS fingerprint to find the tooling
List accounts with a successful login from attacking infrastructure
Check whether successful logins were followed by profile, payment, or address changes
containment: Enable CAPTCHA or proof-of-work challenges on the login endpoint
Block or challenge the attacking ASNs and fingerprints at the WAF
Force password reset and session revoke for accounts that were successfully accessed
Hold orders and withdrawals from compromised accounts pending customer confirmation
eradication: Add the attack's fingerprints to the bot management deny list
Remove attacker-added devices, emails, or phone numbers from compromised accounts
Reverse loyalty, stored value, or settings changes made by the attacker
recovery: Email affected customers with a reset link and guidance on password reuse
Relax challenge levels gradually while watching failure rates
Process refunds for fraudulent orders placed from compromised accounts
lessons: Measure attack duration, compromised account count, and losses
Add a detection on per-ASN login failure ratio
Offer passkeys or MFA to customers and track adoption
Review whether the login API had a weaker path than the web form

splunk.title: Customer login failures and distinct users per minute
splunk.spl: index=web sourcetype=app:auth app=customer-portal action=login | timechart span=1m count(eval(result="failure")) as failures dc(username) as users

splunk.title: Attacking sources ranked by failed logins
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count(eval(Authentication.action="failure")) as fail count(eval(Authentication.action="success")) as ok dc(Authentication.user) as users from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.app=customer-portal by Authentication.src | where users > 20 | sort - fail

splunk.title: Successful logins from attacking IPs
splunk.spl: index=web sourcetype=app:auth app=customer-portal action=login result=success src_ip IN (<attack_ips>) | stats min(_time) as first values(src_ip) as ips by username | convert ctime(first)

playbooks.name: Customer account takeover via SIM swap
playbooks.summary: Use when a customer reports their phone lost service and then their account was accessed via SMS one-time code, password reset, or SMS-based MFA.

preparation: Integrate a carrier SIM-change or number-porting risk signal into login and reset flows
Offer customers authenticator apps or passkeys as alternatives to SMS codes
Log OTP sends and verifications with phone number, carrier, and device ID
identification: Confirm the SIM change date with the customer or the carrier risk API
Review OTP sends and successful verifications for the customer's number after the swap
Identify the device and IP that logged in after OTP verification
Check for email, password, payout, or shipping address changes after takeover
Search for other accounts accessed from the same attacker device ID
containment: Lock the account and revoke every active session and device
Freeze payouts, withdrawals, and order fulfillment on the account
Remove the attacker-added contact details and recovery options
eradication: Block the attacker device fingerprint across the platform
Require a non-SMS factor for the customer before unlocking
Cancel or recall orders shipped to attacker addresses
recovery: Verify the customer through a strong identity check before restoring access
Reimburse losses per policy and record the case for fraud reporting
Apply a temporary hold on high-risk changes for 72 hours after recovery
lessons: Add SIM-change recency as a risk feature in step-up decisions
Count accounts relying solely on SMS for recovery
Review whether support could have blocked the takeover earlier

splunk.title: OTP sends and verifications for the customer number
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=app:otp phone_number="<customer_phone>" | table _time event account_id device_id src_ip carrier result

splunk.title: Account changes after OTP login
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=app:account_audit account_id=<account_id> event IN ("email_change", "password_change", "payout_change", "address_add", "mfa_change") | table _time event old_value new_value device_id src_ip

splunk.title: Other accounts touched by the attacker device
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=app:auth device_id="<attacker_device_id>" | stats dc(account_id) as accounts values(account_id) as ids by device_id

playbooks.name: Loyalty points stolen from customer accounts
playbooks.summary: Use when customers report missing loyalty or rewards points, or analytics show points transferred, redeemed for gift cards, or spent on rapidly shipped goods from taken-over accounts.

preparation: Log every points transfer, redemption, and partner conversion with account and device
Require step-up verification before high-value redemptions or transfers
Notify members by email on each redemption or transfer
identification: List accounts with redemptions from devices never seen before on the account
Map points transfers to receiving accounts to find mule clusters
Identify redemption types used, such as gift cards, partner miles, or digital goods
Check whether redemptions followed a login from credential stuffing infrastructure
containment: Freeze the receiving mule accounts and pending partner conversions
Suspend instant digital redemptions for the affected member tier temporarily
Lock the victim accounts and force password resets
eradication: Cancel unfulfilled gift cards and vouchers issued from stolen points
Close the mule accounts and block their devices and payout details
Ask partners to reverse transferred miles or points where possible
recovery: Restore points to victim accounts per program terms
Send members a notice explaining the restoration and security steps
Re-enable instant redemptions with step-up verification in place
lessons: Quantify points liability lost and recovered
Add a detection for redemptions within an hour of a new-device login
Review partner conversion delays as a fraud control

splunk.title: Redemptions from new devices
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=loyalty:events event=redeem | join type=left account_id device_id [search index=app sourcetype=app:auth result=success earliest=-90d latest=-1d | stats count as seen by account_id device_id] | where isnull(seen) | stats sum(points) as points by account_id device_id redemption_type

splunk.title: Points transfer graph to receiving accounts
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=loyalty:events event=transfer | stats dc(from_account) as senders sum(points) as points by to_account | where senders > 3 | sort - points

playbooks.name: Gift card balances drained by brute force or enumeration
playbooks.summary: Use when gift card balance check or redemption endpoints are hit with many card number and PIN guesses, or customers report gift cards emptied before use.

preparation: Use long random gift card numbers and PINs with no sequential patterns
Rate limit and bot-protect the balance check and redemption endpoints
Log balance checks with card number hash, IP, device, and result
identification: Chart balance check volume and the ratio of invalid to valid card lookups
Identify sources that check many distinct card numbers
List cards with a successful balance check followed by redemption on a new account
Check whether drained cards share a print batch, retailer, or number range
containment: Add CAPTCHA and strict per-IP limits on the balance check endpoint
Freeze balances on cards that were successfully enumerated but not yet redeemed
Block accounts and devices that redeemed enumerated cards
eradication: Cancel and reissue cards from compromised number ranges
Retire the predictable card numbering scheme if it was the cause
Pull physical cards from stores if packaging was tampered with
recovery: Restore balances to legitimate cardholders who present proof of purchase
Reopen the balance checker with bot protection and monitor guess rates
Coordinate with store operations on customer messaging
lessons: Quantify drained value and how much was recovered
Add an alert for invalid balance check ratios above baseline
Review whether gift card entropy meets current guidance

splunk.title: Balance check failure ratio by source
splunk.spl: index=web sourcetype=app:giftcard action=balance_check | stats count(eval(result="invalid")) as invalid count(eval(result="valid")) as valid dc(card_hash) as cards by src_ip | where cards > 50 | eval ratio=round(invalid/(valid+1),1) | sort - cards

splunk.title: Valid lookups followed by redemption
splunk.spl: index=web sourcetype=app:giftcard action IN (balance_check, redeem) result!=invalid | stats values(action) as actions min(_time) as first values(account_id) as accounts by card_hash | where mvcount(actions)=2 | convert ctime(first)

splunk.title: Gift card endpoint traffic in the Web data model
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where Web.uri_path="/api/giftcard/*" by Web.src Web.http_user_agent Web.status _time span=5m

playbooks.name: Card testing attack on checkout
playbooks.summary: Use when checkout or payment authorization sees bursts of small-value attempts with high decline rates, as stolen card numbers are validated through your payment flow.

preparation: Monitor authorization decline rates and decline codes per merchant ID in real time
Enable the payment processor's card testing protections and velocity rules
Keep a contact at the acquirer for attack notification and fee disputes
identification: Chart authorization attempts, decline rate, and average amount per minute
Group attempts by BIN, IP, device fingerprint, and guest versus logged-in checkout
Identify the endpoint used, such as add-card, donation, or zero-dollar auth
List any approved test transactions that would later become chargebacks
containment: Turn on CAPTCHA or 3-D Secure for the targeted payment flow
Block the attacking BIN ranges, IPs, and device fingerprints temporarily
Raise the minimum order value or disable guest checkout during the attack
eradication: Void or refund approved test authorizations before they settle
Close the throwaway accounts created to run the tests
Remove unauthenticated card verification paths that were abused
recovery: Restore normal checkout rules after decline rates return to baseline
Report attack details and tested card ranges to the acquirer
Dispute excess authorization fees with the processor if allowed
lessons: Calculate fees and network fines risked by the attack
Add an alert for decline rate spikes per BIN
Review which payment endpoints lacked bot protection

splunk.title: Authorization attempts and decline rate per minute
splunk.spl: index=payments sourcetype=psp:authorizations | timechart span=1m count as attempts count(eval(status="declined")) as declines avg(amount) as avg_amount

splunk.title: Card testing sources by BIN and device
splunk.spl: index=payments sourcetype=psp:authorizations status=declined | stats dc(card_fingerprint) as cards count by src_ip device_id card_bin | where cards > 10 | sort - cards

splunk.title: Approved low-value auths during the attack window
splunk.spl: index=payments sourcetype=psp:authorizations status=approved amount<5 src_ip IN (<attack_ips>) | table _time transaction_id amount card_bin account_id

playbooks.name: Promo and coupon abuse ring
playbooks.summary: Use when a promotion is being redeemed far above forecast by clusters of new accounts, leaked single-use codes, or scripted code guessing that shares devices and addresses.

preparation: Log every promo redemption with account age, device fingerprint, and shipping address
Set per-device and per-address limits on new-customer promotions
Have marketing share promo terms and expected redemption volumes with fraud
identification: Compare redemptions per hour with the campaign's forecast
Cluster redeeming accounts by device ID, normalized address, and payment fingerprint
Check coupon sites and forums for leaked single-use or employee codes
Detect guessing by counting invalid code attempts per source
containment: Deactivate leaked codes and issue new ones to legitimate recipients
Hold unshipped orders from clustered accounts for review
Enforce one redemption per device and address at checkout
eradication: Cancel orders and revoke credit from accounts in confirmed abuse clusters
Ban the cluster's devices and payment fingerprints from future promos
Replace guessable code formats with long random codes
recovery: Relaunch the promotion with tightened eligibility rules
Honor redemptions for customers wrongly caught in the cluster
Report final promo cost versus budget to marketing
lessons: Measure abuse share of total promo redemptions
Add a pre-launch fraud review step to the campaign process
Track device-cluster detection precision

splunk.title: Promo redemptions per device and address
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=app:orders promo_code="<promo_code>" | eval addr=lower(replace(ship_address, "[^a-zA-Z0-9]", "")) | stats dc(account_id) as accounts by device_id addr | where accounts > 2 | sort - accounts

splunk.title: Invalid promo code attempts by source
splunk.spl: index=web sourcetype=app:checkout event=promo_apply result=invalid | stats dc(promo_code) as codes count by src_ip device_id | where codes > 20

playbooks.name: Fake customer accounts created at scale
playbooks.summary: Use when signups spike from scripted registration using disposable emails, VoIP numbers, or aliasing, to farm bonuses, spam, review fraud, or stage future abuse.

preparation: Score signups using email domain age, disposable domain lists, and phone type
Rate limit and bot-protect the registration and email verification endpoints
Log registration with IP, ASN, device fingerprint, and form fill timing
identification: Chart signups per minute and the share using disposable or aliased emails
Cluster new accounts by device fingerprint, IP range, and name patterns
Identify what the accounts do next: promos, messaging, reviews, or listings
Check whether email or SMS verification is being completed automatically
containment: Add CAPTCHA and email or phone verification before account activation
Block disposable domains and the attacking ASNs at registration
Suspend clustered accounts before they act
eradication: Delete or disable confirmed fake accounts in bulk
Remove spam messages, reviews, or listings the accounts created
Revoke bonuses or credits granted on signup
recovery: Review appeals from legitimate users caught in the sweep
Remove temporary signup friction once rates normalize
Correct marketing and growth metrics inflated by fake signups
lessons: Measure fake account share of signups during the attack
Add a detection for form fill times below human thresholds
Decide whether signup bonuses should vest after real activity

splunk.title: Signup rate and disposable email share
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=app:signup | eval disposable=if(match(email_domain, "(?i)(mailinator|tempmail|guerrillamail)\.example$") OR disposable_flag=1,1,0) | timechart span=5m count sum(disposable) as disposable

splunk.title: Accounts per device fingerprint at signup
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=app:signup earliest=-24h | stats dc(account_id) as accounts values(email_domain) as domains by device_id | where accounts > 5 | sort - accounts

splunk.title: Registration endpoint traffic by ASN
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where Web.uri_path="/register" Web.http_method=POST by Web.src | iplocation Web.src | stats sum(count) as posts by Country Web.src | sort - posts

playbooks.name: Refund fraud or refund-as-a-service abuse
playbooks.summary: Use when refunds are claimed for items reported not received, empty boxes, or returns of different items, often by organized refund services working on buyers' behalf.

preparation: Track refund rate, claim type, and carrier delivery proof per customer
Weigh return parcels at the warehouse and record weight against expected
Give support agents a refund risk score visible in the case tool
identification: List customers whose refund claims exceed peer thresholds in 90 days
Compare item-not-received claims against carrier GPS and photo delivery proof
Find shared scripts, phrasing, or contact numbers in support chats that suggest a refund service
Cluster claimants by device, address, and payment method
containment: Route claims from flagged customers to a specialist review queue
Require returned-item verification before refunding flagged accounts
Pause instant refunds for high-value SKUs being targeted
eradication: Close accounts confirmed to be part of refund fraud per terms of service
File carrier claims or law enforcement reports for organized rings
Update support macros to stop answering known refund-service scripts
recovery: Recover funds through chargeback representment or collections where possible
Re-enable instant refunds with risk-based limits
Brief support agents on the patterns observed
lessons: Calculate refund loss attributable to the ring
Add a detection for weight mismatches on returns
Review whether support incentives encouraged refunds without checks

splunk.title: Customers with high refund claim counts
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=support:refunds earliest=-90d | stats count sum(amount) as total values(claim_type) as claim_types by account_id | where count >= 4 | sort - total

splunk.title: Item-not-received claims with confirmed delivery
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=support:refunds claim_type="not_received" | join order_id [search index=logistics sourcetype=carrier:tracking status=delivered | fields order_id delivery_photo gps_match] | where gps_match="true" | table _time account_id order_id amount delivery_photo

playbooks.name: Support desk socially engineered into handing over a customer account
playbooks.summary: Use when an attacker impersonates a customer to support by chat, phone, or email and gets the email, phone, or MFA changed, then takes over the account.

preparation: Define identity verification steps support must complete before changing contact details
Log every agent-initiated account change with agent ID and case number
Notify the old email and phone whenever support changes account contact details
Record support calls and retain chat transcripts for investigation
identification: Pull the support case, transcript, and recording that led to the change
Identify which verification steps the agent performed or skipped
Check for other cases from the same caller number, email, or chat IP
Review actions taken on the account after support handed over access
containment: Revert the email, phone, and MFA changes and lock the account
Flag the caller's identifiers in the support platform so they are blocked
Freeze balances, payouts, and orders on the account
eradication: Review all changes made by the same agent in the past 30 days for similar cases
Remove any devices the attacker registered after takeover
Close loopholes in verification scripts the attacker exploited
recovery: Restore the real customer's access after strong verification
Reimburse losses and apologize with a clear explanation
Coach the agent and team using the anonymized transcript
lessons: Measure how many attempts the attacker made before succeeding
Add a cooling-off period before high-risk actions after a support change
Track agent override rates of verification failures

splunk.title: Agent-initiated contact detail changes
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=app:account_audit actor_type=agent event IN ("email_change", "phone_change", "mfa_reset") | stats count values(account_id) as accounts by agent_id case_channel | sort - count

splunk.title: Support contacts from the attacker's identifiers
splunk.spl: index=support sourcetype=support:cases (caller_number="<attacker_phone>" OR contact_email="<attacker_email>" OR chat_ip=<ioc_ip>) | table _time case_id account_id channel agent_id outcome

playbooks.name: Customer data scraped through a public or mobile API
playbooks.summary: Use when an API endpoint is enumerated to harvest customer profiles, contact details, or listings, often through an object ID or search endpoint lacking proper authorization.

preparation: Log API requests with API key, account, endpoint, object ID, and response size
Enforce per-key and per-account rate limits on profile and search endpoints
Run authorization tests for object-level access on every API release
identification: Identify API keys or accounts requesting unusually many distinct object IDs
Check whether requested IDs are sequential, which signals enumeration
Confirm which fields the endpoint returned and whether any were private
Estimate the number of customer records retrieved
containment: Revoke the scraping API keys and suspend the associated accounts
Apply strict rate limits or temporarily disable the abused endpoint
Block scraping infrastructure IPs at the API gateway
eradication: Fix the authorization flaw so callers can only read objects they own
Remove private fields from public API responses
Replace sequential IDs with non-guessable identifiers
recovery: Deploy the fix and re-enable the endpoint behind monitoring
Send takedown requests where scraped data is published
Work with legal on customer and regulator notification for private fields
lessons: Add a detection on distinct object IDs per key per hour
Include the endpoint in an API security testing backlog
Review whether the mobile app exposed undocumented endpoints

splunk.title: Distinct object IDs requested per API key
splunk.spl: index=api sourcetype=apigw:access uri_path="/v1/users/*" | rex field=uri_path "/v1/users/(?<obj_id>\d+)" | bin _time span=1h | stats dc(obj_id) as ids sum(bytes_out) as bytes by _time api_key src_ip | where ids > 500

splunk.title: API traffic volume by client
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count sum(Web.bytes_out) as bytes from datamodel=Web where Web.site="api.shop.example" by Web.src Web.http_user_agent | sort - count | head 50

splunk.title: Unauthorized object access responses after the fix
splunk.spl: index=api sourcetype=apigw:access uri_path="/v1/users/*" status IN (403, 404) | timechart span=15m count by api_key limit=10

playbooks.name: Fraudulent password resets on customer accounts
playbooks.summary: Use when attackers abuse the forgot-password flow through weak security questions, reset link leakage, host header poisoning, or compromised customer email to take over accounts.

preparation: Log reset requests, token issuance, and token use with IP and device
Make reset tokens single-use, short-lived, and bound to the requesting session
Notify customers on every completed password reset
identification: Chart reset requests and completions per hour against baseline
Find resets completed from a different IP or device than the request
Test whether the reset flow honors a spoofed Host or X-Forwarded-Host header
Check whether victim email providers or inboxes were compromised first
containment: Invalidate all outstanding reset tokens
Lock accounts reset by attacker infrastructure and revoke sessions
Add step-up verification to the reset flow for risky requests
eradication: Fix any reset link generation that trusts client-supplied host headers
Retire knowledge-based security questions as a sole reset factor
Remove attacker devices and contact changes from affected accounts
recovery: Help customers regain access through verified email or identity check
Reverse orders or transfers made after the fraudulent reset
Monitor reset completion ratios after the fix
lessons: Record how the reset flow was abused and add a regression test
Add a detection for reset completion from a new device and country
Track the share of customers with a second recovery factor

splunk.title: Reset requested and completed from different IPs
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=app:password_reset event IN (requested, completed) | stats values(eval(if(event="requested", src_ip, null()))) as req_ip values(eval(if(event="completed", src_ip, null()))) as done_ip by reset_token_id account_id | where isnotnull(done_ip) AND req_ip!=done_ip

splunk.title: Reset links generated with unexpected host headers
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where Web.uri_path="/forgot-password" Web.http_method=POST by Web.src Web.dest Web.site | where 'Web.site'!="www.shop.example"

playbooks.name: Payment or payout method changed on hijacked accounts
playbooks.summary: Use when attackers add cards, bank accounts, or wallets to taken-over customer accounts, or redirect seller or creator payouts to accounts they control.

preparation: Require step-up verification for adding or changing payout and payment methods
Hold the first payout to a newly added bank account for a review period
Notify customers by email and push when payment details change
identification: List accounts with payout destination changes in the attack window
Find bank accounts or wallets added to multiple unrelated customer accounts
Check whether changes followed new-device logins or contact detail changes
Identify payouts already sent to the new destinations
containment: Freeze pending payouts to the suspicious destinations
Revert payout methods to the last verified destination
Lock affected accounts and revoke sessions
eradication: Block the attacker bank accounts and wallets platform-wide
Request recalls of sent payouts through the payout provider
Report mule accounts to the receiving bank's fraud team
recovery: Pay customers the amounts that were misdirected per policy
Restore access after verification and enrollment in MFA
Release legitimate payouts held during the freeze
lessons: Measure time between payout change and first payout
Add detection for a bank account shared across many customers
Review whether payout change notifications reached customers

splunk.title: Payout destinations shared by many accounts
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=app:account_audit event IN ("payout_method_add", "payout_method_change") | stats dc(account_id) as accounts values(account_id) as ids by payout_fingerprint | where accounts > 1 | sort - accounts

splunk.title: Payout changes following new-device logins
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=app:account_audit event="payout_method_change" | join account_id [search index=app sourcetype=app:auth result=success new_device=true | stats latest(_time) as login_time by account_id] | where _time - login_time < 3600 | table _time account_id payout_fingerprint login_time

splunk.title: Payouts sent to flagged destinations
splunk.spl: index=payments sourcetype=payouts:events payout_fingerprint IN (<flagged_fingerprints>) status IN (sent, pending) | table _time payout_id account_id amount status

playbooks.name: Marketplace seller account takeover
playbooks.summary: Use when a third-party seller's account on your marketplace is taken over to change payout details, list fake bargain items, or message buyers off-platform.

preparation: Require MFA for seller accounts and seller API keys
Hold seller payouts after bank detail changes until verified
Monitor sudden listing changes such as price drops and new categories
identification: Review seller logins, API key creation, and contact detail changes
Find newly created or edited listings with prices far below market
Check buyer messages for links or contact details pushing off-platform payment
List orders placed against the hijacked listings
containment: Suspend new listings and the seller's ability to message buyers
Freeze payouts and revert payout details to the verified bank account
Revoke seller sessions and API keys
eradication: Remove fraudulent listings and restore original catalog data
Warn buyers who received off-platform payment messages
Block attacker devices and IPs across seller and buyer accounts
recovery: Refund buyers of fraudulent orders under marketplace guarantee
Restore the seller's account after verification and MFA enrollment
Reinstate seller ratings affected by fraudulent orders
lessons: Track how many sellers lack MFA and push enrollment
Add detection for listing price drops above a threshold
Review buyer messaging filters for off-platform contact details

splunk.title: Seller account security changes
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=seller:audit seller_id=<seller_id> event IN ("login", "api_key_create", "email_change", "bank_change", "mfa_disable") | table _time event src_ip device_id user_agent

splunk.title: Listings with large price drops
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=catalog:changes field=price | eval drop=round((old_value-new_value)/old_value*100,0) | where drop > 50 | stats count values(listing_id) as listings by seller_id | sort - count

splunk.title: Buyer messages with off-platform contact patterns
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=messaging:events sender_id=<seller_id> | regex body="(?i)(whatsapp|telegram|wire transfer|https?://)" | table _time recipient_id conversation_id

playbooks.name: Phishing site impersonating your brand targets customers
playbooks.summary: Use when a lookalike domain or cloned login page is harvesting your customers' credentials or payment data, discovered via referrer logs, brand monitoring, or customer reports.

preparation: Monitor new domain registrations and certificate transparency logs for brand lookalikes
Embed canary assets or referrer checks so cloned pages show up in web logs
Keep a takedown vendor or registrar abuse contacts ready
Set up DMARC enforcement so the phishing cannot spoof your sending domain
identification: Capture the phishing page screenshot, URL, hosting IP, and registrar details
Search web logs for requests with the phishing domain as referrer
Identify customer accounts that logged in from the phishing site's backend IPs
Determine how the lure is delivered: SMS, email, search ads, or social media
containment: Submit takedown requests to the registrar, host, and certificate authority
Report the URL to browser safe-browsing services and email providers
Force password reset for customers seen authenticating from phishing infrastructure
Block the backend IPs from logging into customer accounts
eradication: Confirm the site is down and track any mirror domains that appear
Request removal of fraudulent search ads using your trademark
Disable canary-asset hotlinking from the cloned page
recovery: Publish a customer notice on known phishing and how to spot it
Reimburse confirmed fraud losses per policy
Continue monitoring for re-registration of similar domains
lessons: Measure time from site launch to takedown
Register high-risk lookalike domains defensively
Add a detection for logins from IPs seen loading the phishing site

splunk.title: Requests referred from the phishing domain
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where Web.http_referrer="*<phish_domain>*" by Web.src Web.uri_path Web.http_referrer

splunk.title: Customer logins from phishing backend IPs
splunk.spl: index=web sourcetype=app:auth app=customer-portal src_ip IN (<phish_backend_ips>) | stats count values(result) as results by username src_ip | sort - count

playbooks.name: Fake mobile app impersonating your brand
playbooks.summary: Use when a counterfeit app using your name or logo appears in an app store or sideload site and collects customer logins, payment data, or pushes malware.

preparation: Monitor Google Play, the App Store, and third-party stores for apps using your brand
Register trademarks so store intellectual property complaints can be filed fast
Use app attestation so your API can tell your genuine app from clones
identification: Record the fake app's store listing, developer name, package ID, and install count
Analyze the app in a sandbox to find credential capture or backend endpoints
Check API logs for requests with the fake app's package ID or failed attestation
Identify customer accounts that logged in through the fake app
containment: File impersonation and IP complaints with the app store
Block API requests that fail app attestation or use the clone's signature
Reset credentials for customers who used the fake app
eradication: Request takedown of the backend domains the fake app talks to
Report sideload hosting sites to their providers
Rotate any API keys the fake app extracted from your genuine app
recovery: Tell customers which app is official and link to the genuine listing
Confirm the fake listing is removed and watch for re-uploads
Reimburse losses for customers defrauded through the app
lessons: Measure installs before takedown and time to removal
Add brand monitoring alerts for new developer accounts using your name
Review whether embedded secrets in your app helped the clone

splunk.title: API calls from non-genuine app builds
splunk.spl: index=api sourcetype=apigw:access (app_package!="com.shop.example" OR attestation_result!="pass") | stats count dc(account_id) as accounts by app_package app_signature attestation_result

splunk.title: Customers logging in through the fake app
splunk.spl: index=web sourcetype=app:auth client_package="<fake_package_id>" result=success | stats min(_time) as first by username src_ip | convert ctime(first)

playbooks.name: Sudden spike in chargebacks
playbooks.summary: Use when chargeback or dispute counts jump above normal, risking card network monitoring programs, and the cause could be stolen cards, friendly fraud, or a billing problem.

preparation: Report chargeback ratio per merchant ID daily against network thresholds
Store order evidence such as IP, device, delivery proof, and 3-D Secure results
Keep a clear billing descriptor and customer service contact on statements
identification: Break disputes down by reason code, BIN country, product, and order date
Check whether disputed orders share devices, IPs, or shipping addresses
Rule out a billing bug such as duplicate charges or unclear subscription renewals
Compare the dispute timeline with known card testing or ATO incidents
containment: Turn on 3-D Secure for the risky BINs, products, or regions driving disputes
Hold shipment of orders matching the fraud pattern for manual review
Refund likely-fraudulent recent orders before they become chargebacks
eradication: Block the devices, cards, and addresses linked to fraud disputes
Fix billing descriptors or renewal emails if friendly fraud is the cause
Close accounts confirmed to be part of the fraud pattern
recovery: Submit representment evidence for disputes that can be won
Inform the acquirer of the remediation plan if near a monitoring threshold
Track the chargeback ratio daily until it is back under target
lessons: Measure dispute loss and fees for the period
Add an alert when the daily dispute ratio crosses an internal threshold
Review whether fraud screening rules missed the pattern

splunk.title: Disputes by reason code and BIN country
splunk.spl: index=payments sourcetype=psp:disputes earliest=-30d | stats count sum(amount) as amount by reason_code card_country | sort - count

splunk.title: Daily chargeback ratio
splunk.spl: index=payments (sourcetype=psp:disputes OR sourcetype=psp:authorizations status=approved) earliest=-60d | eval kind=if(sourcetype="psp:disputes", "dispute", "sale") | timechart span=1d count(eval(kind="dispute")) as disputes count(eval(kind="sale")) as sales | eval ratio_pct=round(disputes/sales*100,2)

playbooks.name: Crypto withdrawals from hijacked customer accounts
playbooks.summary: Use when a crypto exchange or wallet platform sees taken-over customer accounts whitelisting new addresses and withdrawing assets, often after API key creation or MFA reset.

preparation: Apply a time lock after new withdrawal address whitelisting or security setting changes
Require hardware key or passkey confirmation for withdrawals above limits
Subscribe to a blockchain analytics service for address risk and tracing
Keep contacts at other exchanges for freeze requests
identification: List accounts that added withdrawal addresses or created API keys from new devices
Trace withdrawal transactions on-chain to destination clusters
Check whether withdrawals followed MFA reset, email change, or support interaction
Identify the attacker's common destination addresses across victims
containment: Pause withdrawals for accounts showing the takeover pattern
Disable API keys created during the attack window
Block the destination addresses platform-wide
eradication: Remove attacker-added whitelist addresses and devices from accounts
Request freezes from exchanges where funds landed, with transaction hashes
Report the theft to law enforcement with on-chain tracing evidence
recovery: Restore account access after identity verification and new MFA
Decide on customer reimbursement per terms and insurance
Lift withdrawal pauses once each account is verified
lessons: Quantify assets lost and frozen
Add detection for whitelist changes followed by max withdrawals
Review whether the address time lock was long enough

splunk.title: Whitelist additions followed by withdrawals
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=exchange:audit event IN ("address_whitelist_add", "withdrawal_request") | stats values(event) as events min(_time) as first max(_time) as last sum(amount_usd) as usd by account_id | where mvcount(events)=2 AND last-first < 86400 | sort - usd

splunk.title: Common destination addresses across accounts
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=exchange:withdrawals status IN (sent, pending) earliest=-7d | stats dc(account_id) as victims sum(amount_usd) as usd by dest_address asset | where victims > 1 | sort - usd

splunk.title: API keys created from new devices
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=exchange:audit event="api_key_create" new_device=true | table _time account_id key_id permissions src_ip device_id

playbooks.name: Account sharing and resale of customer accounts
playbooks.summary: Use when subscription or premium accounts are shared beyond terms or resold on marketplaces, shown by many concurrent devices, geographies, or bulk-created premium accounts.

preparation: Track concurrent sessions and distinct devices per account
Define the sharing limits in terms of service and the enforcement steps
Monitor resale marketplaces and forums for listings of your accounts
identification: Identify accounts with concurrent streams or sessions from distant locations
Find accounts with device counts far above the plan limit
Match accounts against resale listings using trial patterns or credentials posted
Check whether resold accounts were obtained by ATO or by stolen payment cards
containment: Enforce concurrent session limits on flagged accounts
Sign out all devices on accounts confirmed as resold
Report resale listings to the marketplace hosting them
eradication: Return taken-over accounts to their real owners with a forced reset
Cancel accounts paid for with stolen cards and refund cardholders
Block bulk-creation payment fingerprints tied to resellers
recovery: Offer legitimate sharers an upgrade path to family or multi-seat plans
Monitor complaints from customers affected by enforcement
Relax concurrent session enforcement for accounts cleared on appeal
lessons: Estimate revenue lost to sharing and resale
Add a detection for impossible-travel concurrent sessions per account
Decide whether device limits should be tightened per plan

splunk.title: Accounts with many devices and countries
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=app:sessions earliest=-7d | iplocation src_ip | stats dc(device_id) as devices dc(Country) as countries by account_id plan | where devices > 10 OR countries > 3 | sort - devices

splunk.title: Concurrent sessions per account
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=app:sessions event=heartbeat | bin _time span=5m | stats dc(device_id) as concurrent by _time account_id | where concurrent > 4 | stats max(concurrent) as peak by account_id

playbooks.name: Bots buying up tickets or limited-release items
playbooks.summary: Use when scalper bots buy most of a ticket drop or limited product release, shown by checkout bursts, queue bypass, many accounts per payment instrument, or resale listings minutes later.

preparation: Put a virtual waiting room and bot management in front of drop pages and checkout
Set per-customer, per-card, and per-address purchase limits for limited items
Pre-agree with merchandising when orders may be cancelled for bot activity
identification: Measure time from drop start to checkout for each order
Find orders that bypassed the waiting room or called checkout APIs directly
Cluster buyers by payment fingerprint, address variations, and device
Check resale marketplaces for listings that appeared during the drop
containment: Raise bot challenge levels on checkout and add-to-cart endpoints
Hold fulfillment of orders in suspicious clusters
Block direct API calls that skip the queue token
eradication: Cancel bot-driven orders and release inventory back to the queue
Ban accounts and payment fingerprints confirmed as bots
Fix the queue bypass so checkout requires a valid waiting room token
recovery: Re-sell released inventory through a verified fan or raffle process
Communicate with customers about fair access measures
Return waiting room and bot challenge settings to normal after the drop closes
lessons: Measure bot share of purchases during the drop
Add pre-drop load and bot testing to the release checklist
Review address normalization so variants are caught

splunk.title: Checkout speed after drop start
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=app:orders sku IN (<limited_skus>) | eval secs_after_drop=_time-strptime("<drop_time>", "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S") | stats count by account_id device_id secs_after_drop | where secs_after_drop < 10

splunk.title: Checkout requests without a queue token
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where Web.uri_path="/api/checkout" Web.http_method=POST by Web.src Web.http_user_agent | join type=left Web.src [search index=web sourcetype=waitingroom:events event=token_issued | rename src_ip as Web.src | stats count as tokens by Web.src] | where isnull(tokens)

splunk.title: Orders per payment fingerprint
splunk.spl: index=app sourcetype=app:orders sku IN (<limited_skus>) | stats dc(account_id) as accounts sum(quantity) as units by card_fingerprint | where accounts > 2 | sort - units

playbooks.name: Synthetic identities passing customer onboarding
playbooks.summary: Use when KYC or credit onboarding approves applicants built from mixed real and fake identity data, often surfaced by bust-out losses, shared SSNs or phones, or document verification gaps.

preparation: Use document verification with liveness checks for regulated onboarding
Check identity attributes against consortium data and SSA eCBSV where available
Log all onboarding attributes and verification vendor results for later linkage
identification: Link approved applicants that share SSNs, phones, emails, addresses, or devices
Find identities with thin credit files that grew quickly and then maxed out
Review document verification results for template reuse or edited images
Estimate exposure: credit lines, balances, and pending transactions
containment: Freeze credit lines and outbound transfers on linked suspect accounts
Pause automated approvals for the onboarding segment being abused
Flag the shared attributes so new applications using them go to manual review
eradication: Close confirmed synthetic accounts and file suspicious activity reports as required
Report synthetic identities to credit bureaus and fraud consortiums
Tune onboarding rules to reject the identified attribute patterns
recovery: Resume automated approvals with the new linkage checks in place
Handle real individuals whose SSNs were misused and correct their records
Charge off unrecoverable balances and record them as fraud losses
lessons: Quantify losses and how long synthetic accounts aged before bust-out
Add a graph detection for attributes shared across approved customers
Review vendor verification performance on the confirmed cases

splunk.title: Approved applicants sharing identity attributes
splunk.spl: index=onboarding sourcetype=kyc:applications decision=approved | stats dc(customer_id) as customers values(customer_id) as ids by ssn_hash | where customers > 1 | append [search index=onboarding sourcetype=kyc:applications decision=approved | stats dc(customer_id) as customers values(customer_id) as ids by phone_hash | where customers > 2]

splunk.title: Rapid credit utilization after account aging
splunk.spl: index=lending sourcetype=credit:accounts | eval age_days=round((now()-open_time)/86400) | where utilization_pct > 90 AND age_days < 365 | table customer_id age_days credit_limit balance utilization_pct

splunk.title: Document verification results with reused templates
splunk.spl: index=onboarding sourcetype=idv:results | stats dc(customer_id) as customers by document_template_hash result | where customers > 3
